related_questions.question: Can you fix brittle bone disease?
related_questions.snippet: To date, there is no known treatment, medicine, or surgery that will cure osteogenesis imperfecta (OI). The goal of treatment is to prevent deformities and fractures and allow the child to function as independently as possible. Treatments for preventing or correcting symptoms may include: Care of fractures.

related_questions.question: What is the main cause of brittle bones?
related_questions.snippet: For most people, a change or defect in the genes that carry the instructions for making type I collagen causes OI. Type I collagen is a material in bones that helps make them strong. The defect in the genes causes the body to make collagen incorrectly or not make enough, leading to weak bones that break more easily.

related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of a person with brittle bones?
related_questions.snippet: Life expectancy People with the most severe forms of brittle bone disease may die during infancy. However, most people who receive supportive care and medical management can expect to lead healthy, productive lives with average life span.

text_blocks.snippet: Brittle bone disease, also known as Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI), is primarily caused by genetic mutations affecting the production of collagen, a protein crucial for bone strength and structure. These mutations can lead to either insufficient collagen production or the production of abnormal collagen, making bones weaker and more susceptible to fractures.
snippet_highlighted_words: genetic mutations affecting the production of collagen

list.title: Type I Collagen:
list.snippet: In most cases, OI is caused by mutations in genes responsible for producing type I collagen, a major component of bone and other connective tissues.

list.title: Inheritance:
list.snippet: These mutations can be inherited from a parent (dominant or recessive inheritance) or can occur spontaneously as a new mutation in the affected individual.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: The specific mutation and its impact on collagen production influence the severity of OI, ranging from mild to severe.

list.title: Bone Structure:
list.snippet: Collagen provides the framework for bone mineralization, giving it strength and flexibility.

list.title: Other Tissues:
list.snippet: Collagen is also found in other connective tissues like tendons, ligaments, skin, and even the sclera (white of the eye).

list.title: Defective Collagen:
list.snippet: Mutations can result in insufficient collagen, collagen that is not properly formed, or collagen that is not properly incorporated into the bone matrix.

list.title: Vitamin D Deficiency:
list.snippet: In some cases, severe vitamin D deficiency can contribute to bone fragility, but this is distinct from OI.

list.title: Rickets:
list.snippet: Rickets, a childhood condition, also involves bone softening due to deficiencies in calcium, vitamin D, or phosphate, but it is not the same as OI.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, OI is primarily a genetic disorder that affects the quality and quantity of collagen, leading to fragile bones that break easily.
